model.rationale: All the visible xrpl imports exist in xrpl 5.3.0, and the project passes strict typechecking. These include the MPT flag enums, encodeMPTokenMetadata/validateMPTokenMetadata, RippledError, decodeAccountID and the MPTAmount/MPTokenMetadata types. The request fields also exist (tx with min_ledger/max_ledger, submit tx_blob, searched_all), as do the transaction fields (MPTokenAuthorize with tfMPTUnauthorize=1 and MPT Payment Amount). The only doubtful item is the locally defined lsfMPTCanHoldConfidentialBalance (0x80); I can't confirm that name, but it is not an xrpl.js API and is only used to check that the flag is absent. Part of issuer.ts was truncated, so I couldn't review all of it.

Error 4 is a TS2724 compiler error: the agent imported 'MPTokenIssuanceFlags' from xrpl, but xrpl doesn't export that name (the compiler suggested 'MPTokenIssuanceSetFlags'). So the agent used an xrpl.js export that does not exist.

The code uses current xrpl 5.x APIs (MPT flag enums, encode/validateMPTokenMetadata, autofill/sign/submit/tx requests, getLedgerIndex, and Wallet.fromSeed with the new inferred key type). Nothing in the visible code is listed as deprecated or removed; setTransactionFlagsToNumber is not used. src/issuer.ts was truncated, so not all of it could be checked.
The strict-forced tsc run (every strict-family option on, noCheck off, all sources listed) exited 0 with 0 errors, and so did the project's own strict config.
Visible code has two `as unknown as` casts in test/unit.test.ts (fake metadata, and a number passed as a string). src/issuer.ts is truncated, so it may contain more.
Every transaction goes through submitOrThrow/requireSuccess or returns a validated result that the demo asserts on. Visible code never treats a submission as done without checking the result.
submitAndConfirm polls the tx command until validated, and only reports expiry after a complete search of the LastLedgerSequence window.
Amounts are built as { mpt_issuance_id, value: bigint.toString() } in base units. The demo uses assetScale 0, so no scaling is needed.
The seed is read from the ISSUER_SEED environment variable, loaded from .env; no source file contains it.
Both the demo and verify scripts call client.disconnect() in a finally block.
The demo asserts the ban claws back the full balance, de-authorizes C on the ledger, records C in the registry, and blocks later re-authorize/issue/unfreeze; re-applying it re-freezes C.
The issuance is created with tfMPTCanLock, MPTokenIssuanceSetFlags is imported, and the demo shows per-holder and global freezes taking effect on the ledger. The implementation itself is truncated.
The issuance has tfMPTCanClawback, the MPTAmount type is used, and clawedBackAmount reads a specific holder's MPToken entry. The implementation is truncated, so this is inferred.
